column4: Visit note | 2025-05-08 02:30 PM | Dr. Rezaul Karim, Neurology | Patient: Laila Khatun, 76, female. Mrs. Khatun mentions she gets dizzy whenever she looks up, accompanied by nausea during the spinning sensations. She states this started after a long bus ride to Jatrabari. She works as a shopkeeper and lives with her family. She has a history of Essential hypertension. She denies weakness, fainting spells, double vision, or hearing loss. On examination: Dix-Hallpike test positive on the right side, BP 139/86 mmHg, pulse 76 bpm, weight 62 kg. Cranial nerves are intact and cerebellar signs are absent. Assessment: Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to get up slowly from bed, avoid sudden head movements, and repeat the Epley manoeuvre at home as shown. Follow-up in 2 weeks.
